title: Worms Get Ready to Fly in Space

image.attribution: Dan Dickinson, Goldstein lab, UNC Chapel Hill / http://wormcas9hr.weebly.com / CC-BY-SA 3.0

main_content:
Humans are well-equipped for life on Earth. But in space, it is a different story. Low or zero gravity changes how the blood flows and causes motion sickness, muscle loss and tiredness. But scientists at the University of Delaware are experimenting with little worms to better understand how space travel affects astronauts.

The millimeter-long worm is called C. elegans. The see-through invertebrate is often used in medical studies because its life is only about two weeks long. Seventy percent of its DNA is the same as human DNA.

Chandran Sabanayagam is a scientist with the University of Delaware. He built a micro-gravity simulator to test how C. elegans would perform in the actual zero gravity of space.

Scientists use a computer to watch the worms as they turn. The computer shows the worms as they would look under a microscope. Mr. Sabanayagam says the worms turn around and around in the simulator for about one week.

After about a week the scientists take out the worms. They look for changes in the worms’ epigenome. The epigenome are chemical markers that tell the DNA in the cells how to perform. The epigenome can be changed by the environment. And those changes pass from one generation of worms to the next.

Chandran Sabanayagam expects C. elegans to visit the International Space Station within two years. He says he hopes information gathered from the worm studies can be used to develop simple, low-cost and quick tests to measure an astronaut’s health.

questions.question: What can low or zero gravity do to humans and their health?
options: It enhances muscle growth and improves blood flow.
It increases the risk of developing chronic diseases.
It causes motion sickness, muscle loss, and tiredness.
It has no significant effect on human health.
questions.answer: It causes motion sickness, muscle loss, and tiredness.

questions.question: Who built the micro-gravity simulator?
options: A team of scientists from NASA.
Chandran Sabanayagam from the University of Delaware.
An unknown researcher studying space effects.
A group of graduate students at a local college.
questions.answer: Chandran Sabanayagam from the University of Delaware.

questions.question: What is an epigenome?
options: The genetic blueprint of an organism.
Chemical markers that influence DNA behavior.
The physical structure of cells in the body.
A type of mutation that occurs in DNA.
questions.answer: Chemical markers that influence DNA behavior.
